A tile clot whose
grain changes with its whereabouts.
A little darker and
more deeply hued than the
game's everyday clay tiles.

Corner decking for clinker
walls. Set it while
looking level to
deck the corner of
a building. Look nearly
straight up or down
to deck a window.
It first follows the
shape of nearby
Sandstone-Decked Clots, easing the
work on taller buildings.

A halfclot made from
clinker tiles. A little
darker and more deeply hued
than everyday clay tiles.

A tile clot whose
grain changes with its whereabouts.
A little darker and more
deeply hued than everyday
clay tiles, with clearer
marks of grime and smut.
A halfclot made from grimy clinker tiles.

A little darker and
more deeply hued than everyday
clay tiles, with clearer marks
of grime and smut.

A little darker and

A plain wall of clinker tiles.

A smoking stack that fits the
Dark Shingle Roof Smokestack Foot. Click
to change how much smoke rises.

A foot for a smokestack
or an IE Wire Link,
bringing RF might into
the building through the roof.

Hard-packed earthy ground, with a
plain grain and a few
cracks, much like a well-trodden
path or yard. Mix Dirt
and Rough Dirt into it
for further detail. The grain
changes with its whereabouts, and
grass cannot spread onto it.

Hard-packed sandy ground mixed
with small stones, such as
the ground in loom yards
and stockyards. Flowers hardly
grow on it. Its
grain changes with its whereabouts.

A dropper for well-built self-working
worksteads. Its twelve slots are
picked one after another. Sliders on
the screen set throwing strength,
slant, heap size and waiting
time. Three heap-matching slots below
the inholding slots can start
it from within, using AND
or OR. Join this inward starter
to the outer redstone starter
with AND or OR as
well. The shutter opens early
when it is ready to
throw and awaiting the outer
token. All matching heaps are thrown
together. Hover over knaps for
2s to read their hints.

Throwing way x/y (-45° to +45°)§r
§7See the green-red waymarks on the fore side.

How the outer token joins in§r
§9AND§7: Throw only upon an outer token.
§9OR§7: Throw matching heaps by themselves; other things need the outer starter.
§9IGNORE§7: Heed no outer Redstone, as though the outer starter were always on.

How the sieves work together§r
§9AND§7: Throw the heaps named by the sieves only when ALL sieves are green.
§9OR§7: Throw each sieve's heap when that sieve is green.

Outer Redstone token light
§7(click to start it by hand).

Starting kind§r
§9Beat§7: Throw once for each OFF->ON of the outer token.
§9Unbroken§7: Keep throwing while the outer token stays ON.

Throwing speed (slow to fast)
§7The spring is loose at the bottom and tight at the top.

A hopper for well-built self-working worksteads.
It can shift half-heaps and gather
over at most 9x9. Screen sliders
set gathering reach (0 to 4),
the wait between inward shifts (0.5s
to 10s), and inward heap size
(1 to 32). Screen redstone settings:
straight or flipped (the starting choice),
beat or unbroken (the starting choice).
Heap to put in §7(1 to 32 things)

Waiting light
§7Blinks while the inward-shift timer is still running, or when the Hopper cannot put things into the next inholding.

Sets clots and plants crops or
trees. Screen redstone settings: straight
or flipped (the starting choice), beat
or unbroken (the starting choice). Crop
seeds are planted in free room
above Cropland. Things it cannot
set or plant are spat out.
Outer token §7(click to run one setting round)

Stock row 3§r
§7Click to start setting from the bottom stock row.

Stock row 2§r
§7Click to start setting from the middle stock row.

Stock row 1§r
§7Click to start setting from the top stock row.

with a small built-in height reader
using a thrutch pipe. It stands
upright when set; sneak while setting
it to choose another way.
A standing barrel feeds flowstuff into
vats below. It can be filled
or drained while held as a
thing, and sends a Bemeter token.

A thin sliver that stacks upright.
With a heap of slivers in hand,
right- or left-click the top or bottom
to add or take away slivers.

A small glowstone light
for overhead clots, walls, edder
posts or bloom poles.

A small glowstone light
set on the edge
of an overhead clot.

A small glowstone light set
at the edge of
a floor clot. Helpful for
lighting spots where leveny
lights are hard to fit.

An upside-down trapdoor above
upkeep shafts or ladders.
Creeper-proof, and climbable like
a ladder when open.

A small glowstone light sunk
into the floor, an overhead
clot or a wall. Helpful
for lighting spots where leveny
lights are hard to fit.

An everyday workstead wall
ladder with level bloom-rod
rungs. Look up or
down to climb faster.

Staggered rod rungs fixed to a
wall for climbing up, dropping
down and so on. Look
up or down to climb faster.

Strengthened glass, dear to
make but blast-proof. Dark
gray, with faint frame
lines and sundry grains
for an unbroken look.

Strengthened glass in a
halfclot, dear to make
but blast-proof. Dark gray,
with faint frame lines.

Stonelime strengthened with steel.
Dear to make, but Creeper/Wither-proof.

A stonelime halfclot strengthened with steel.
Dear to make, but Creeper/Wither-proof.

Stonelime stairs strengthened with steel.
Dear to make, but Creeper/Wither-proof.

A stonelime tile strengthened with steel.
Dear to make, but Creeper-proof.

steel. Dear to make, but Creeper-proof.

Dear to make, but Creeper-proof.

Dear to make, but Creeper-proof.
A plain workstead markboard sheet for workshop names, show walls and workstead markings.
The door is over there, if you please ...

A warning of leveny harm. Do
not forget to set it
around HV, or the next
check will find your work wanting.

A gray-brown tile clot whose
grain changes with its whereabouts.
A plain wall of slag tiles.
Breaks clots before its working side. A redstone token can stop it. Working speed depends on the clot being broken.

A small bloom-cased through-flow kiln. It
draws things from the inward
side and puts things into the
inholding on the outward side.
Hoppers can add or take things
from any side. Things that cannot
be smelted or cooked go
straight through. It is a little
thriftier and faster than a
burning Cobblestone Kiln. FIFO rows and
feeders shift whole heaps; feeders need
a little might. Put a
Hopper in a helper slot to
draw things on its own
from inholdings on the inward side.

Helper slot
§7Put a Hopper here to draw things from the inward side by itself.

Gathers flowstuff from above. Its
inner vat holds three buckets.
It follows flowing stuff back
to nearby spring clots. Take
the flowstuff with flow-carrying works
or a bucket. It fills
only vats below, letting the
flow fall downward. It works
with the game's endless-water-spring making.

An ice-making loom. Cools water
to Ice, then Packed Ice,
then Bloe Ice. Click with
a water bucket or
pipe water in, and feed
it RF might. Take the
wanted ice kind with a
Hopper or other thing-drawing means.
Cut off RF or send
a redstone token to
stop the freezer. A Redstone
Bemeter can read the current
ice step for self-running works.

A small bloom-cased tryout kiln. It
burns solid stuff and draws air upward.
It is a little hotter and
keeps heat better than a Cobblestone
Kiln, making it thriftier. Two helper
slots can hold stock. Inner hopper FIFO
rows hold two heaps each for
things coming in, things going out
and burning stuff. Put an outside
heater in a helper slot and feed
it might for faster leveny smelting.

Milks cows from time to
time and has an inner flowstuff
vat. It does not feed
the beasts. Take milk with buckets.
It draws empty milk holders
from inholdings behind or below
and puts full ones back. It
first seeks empties behind and
room below, but can put full
holders back in the same
inholding. It sends milk to
vats or pipes below only if
milk is a flowstuff. Do
not crowd the cow pen: only
happy beasts come by willingly.

A very hot leveny stone
melter that holds heat well.§r
Heats stone clots into
Moltenstone Clots and lastly Moltenstone.
Click with a stone clot,
such as Stone or Cobblestone,
or feed one in as
a thing. Take Moltenstone
with a bucket or flowstuff
draw. Cooling Moltenstone makes Ravenglass.
Cut off RF or send
a redstone token to stop
the kiln. A Redstone
Bemeter can read the stone's
melting step for self-running works.

Makes a little might in sunlight.
Helpful for loading LF might holders
in faraway works that use
little might. Its inner load-pumping loop
gathers RF and sends it onward
often. Yield depends on the time
of day and the weather. Click
to see how full it
is, how much it makes and
how far the work has gone.
Cuts grown trees before its working side. It does not gather their drops. Send a redstone token to stop it.

An offal bin with inner
FIFO slots. Feed things in
from any side. They stay
until the FIFO has no
room left; the oldest heap
is then burned. Feed RF/FE
might to speed up the
work. Its inholding stays with
it when it is moved.

A plain walkway for reaching big
looms. From above, it can also be
set in the way you are looking.
Click with a Guardrail to add
a rail to one side: a
near click picks the spot, while a
far click finds the best fit. Click
again to take a rail away.

Click with a Steel Guardrail to
add or take away rails. Cannot
be set with the bottom facing
down; no corners (unlike everyday Stairs).

A walkway lined up with the
top, joining steel poles beneath it.
A short, level beam for holding up overhead clots.

Steel decking for floors, lined up
with the top. Things fall through it.

A steel-framed window with three layers
of glass. Set it in a
1-clot wall gap. It uses steel sheets
from the Bloom Workbench crafting path.

A workstead-style edder. Does
not join everyday edders. Joins
whole clots when lined up
with another mesh edder.

A workstead-style gate that
fits the Steel Mesh
Edder. Set it as a
one-wide or two-wide gate.

A decking guardrail. Add or
take away sides by clicking
with guardrails in hand.
Also works on Steel Walkways.
A strong steel table with four legs.

A straight bit of flowstuff pipe.
Lets flowstuff through only one way, with
no links to the sides. Slows
the flow. Sneak while setting it to
turn the flow the other way.

A straight bit of flowstuff pipe.
Lets flowstuff through only one way,
with no links to the sides.
Sneak while setting it to turn
the flow the other way. Shuts
when there is no redstone might.

A straight bit of flowstuff pipe.
Lets flowstuff through only one way, with
no links to the sides. Sneak
while setting it to turn the
flow the other way. Shuts without redstone
might; the flow is held below
full and rises by even steps
from might 1 to 14, reaching the
gate's fullest flow at might 15.

A straight, hollow
pole bit (6x6x16) for
holding up builds.

A steel fitting for the foot or
head of the thick steel pole (6x6x16).

A straight, hollow pole bit
(4x4x16) for holding up builds.
Craft it from steel sheets
made at the Bloom Workbench.

A steel fitting for the foot or
head of the thin steel pole (4x4x16).
Decking floor tiles with sundry grains.

A straight pole bit as
wide as a wire relay.
A helpful stand-in for wire posts
when other lengths are needed,
or for holding up builds.

A wooden fitting for the foot
or head of straight poles.

A strong wooden brace
for the foot or
head of straight poles.
For when the work is over.

A strong wood stool
for indoors or outdoors.

A mark that sends a
redstone beat into its backing
clot when an arrow
hits it or it is
started by hand. Click with
a Redstone Brand to
set the outflow, stepping through
the choices this switch offers.

A player watcher fixed to
the wall above a door.§r

Points up, down or
both ways, depending on where
you click the wall
when setting it. A switch
that sends a short
redstone token, much like
a knap. Click with a
Redstone Brand to set
the outflow, stepping through the
choices this switch offers.

A switch that sends a
short redstone token, much
like a knap. Click with
a Redstone Brand to set
the outflow, stepping through the
choices this switch offers.
While it is already on,
start it again to lengthen
the beat. Left-click with
a heap of redstone to
set a fixed beat length
from 0.1s (1) to 6.4s
(64). Left-click with any
dye to hue the switch.

A glass floor sheet that
changes hue and sends a
redstone token when something
weighs on its top, such
as someone standing on it,
and for a short while
after that weight is
lifted. Sends forward and downward.
Makes no sound. Feels even
light touches. Click with a
Redstone Brand to set the
outflow, stepping through the
choices this switch offers. Left-click
with a heap of redstone
to set the hold time
from 0.1s (1) to
6.4s (64). Left-click with any
dye to hue the switch.

A small glass loom that
sends a redstone token
from a chosen start time
to a chosen end
time. Fore-side knaps set the
span with a 24-hour clock,
where 06:00 means sunrise.
They also set the outflow
strength and a haphazard-wait value.
The latter adds a
haphazard wait before turning on
or off; higher values
mean longer waits. Sends into
its backing clot. Makes no
switching sounds. Click with
a Redstone Brand to set
the outflow, stepping through
the choices this switch offers.

A glass floor sheet that

the outflow, stepping through the
choices this switch offers. Left-click
with a heap of redstone
to set the hold
time from 0.1s (1) to
6.4s (64). Left-click with any

jei.info.immersive_engineer_decor_contro: An Athamans-grade sareman's manytool. Sets Brands from your inholding, works as an axe, shovel, tiller and shears while sneaking, fells linked logs when sneak-breaking, and can be mended or overmended with Athamans in crafting.

Lore: Stores a target world-room and block stead on use. Sneak-use clears the stored target, and the helptext shows the saved stead when one is complete.
A single-heap marking tool with 100 uses. Setting it rightly adds an arrow mark to a sturdy side and wears the tool; a failed try does not wear it.
Lore: Emergency healing tool. It can be used manually, and it can auto-trigger at low health to grant short survival effects before entering cooldown.
Lore: Carryable overworld sleep tool. It advances a safe night to morning without setting spawn and refuses unsafe or non-night use.
Lore: Stores up to 512 of one plain, heapable stuff type. Hold the box in main hand with matching stuff in off hand to load it, or use it with an empty off hand to retrieve stuff.
Lore: Emergency air capsule. It can refill air manually or auto-trigger at low air, then enters cooldown.
Lore: Hand tool for compact rations. It consumes bread, an apple, and an accepted seed to create four Muslee Bars when outcome space is available.
Lore: Fast engineer ration produced by the Muslee Bar Press or its crafting.
Turns Hewnstone into Loaded Hewnstone by spending one XP level and a little health, and making you weary in a way that brings hunger. Will not work when health is low.

Sareman's tool stuff used by the rebuilt crafting set.
